original_value: Datacenter operators need efficient methods to diagnose anomalous network behavior and performance stragglers across large clusters. This article presents Merlin, a causal sketching framework that combines interpretable statistical inference with lightweight traffic measurement to identify root causes from job traces and packet-level summaries. The approach targets large-scale production environments, supports both per-flow and aggregate analysis, and emphasizes low-overhead deployment, unbiased diagnosis, and practical tradeoffs between accuracy and space. Experiments on warehouse-scale traces and distributed analytics workloads illustrate how the framework can help isolate bottlenecks, contention, and misconfigured resources in modern datacenters.

result.paraphrase: This article introduces Merlin, a causal sketching framework for spotting anomalous network behavior and slow outliers in large clusters. It blends interpretable statistical inference with lightweight traffic measurements to infer root causes from job traces and packet-level summaries. Designed for large-scale production environments, it supports both per-flow and aggregate analysis while prioritizing low overhead, unbiased diagnosis, and practical accuracy-versus-space tradeoffs. Experiments on warehouse-scale traces and distributed analytics workloads show how it can help isolate bottlenecks, contention, and misconfigured resources in modern datacenters.
